clarity.justification: The sweep-and-probe procedure is understandable—“fit a linear probe ... to classify valid vs breakdown regime,” localize a transition, and compare it with a stated boundary—but several examples do not define a unique scientific boundary: “breaks near critical point,” “Michaelis-Menten linear regime vs saturation (Vmax),” and “below ~0.1 concentration regime” conflate gradual, system-dependent deviations with fixed boundary values. More seriously, high boundary AUROC can arise because representations encode the swept scalar rather than an applicability judgment, and the listed “random-direction and shuffled-label nulls” do not distinguish those explanations; the proposed DVS aggregation is also unspecified. The prediction that “some models mark breakdown regimes cleanly while others extrapolate blindly” has no model-specific direction or numeric decision threshold, so virtually any heterogeneous result fits it and there is no clear overall outcome that refutes the hypothesis.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is constructing semantically valid “temperature-annotated sequences” and “concentration-annotated molecules” with corresponding model outputs and ground-truth boundaries; this is underdefined because ChemBERTa, MolFormer, and ESM-2 exist but their standard inputs do not directly encode those experimental conditions or predict all the proposed law-deviation curves. Activation extraction, linear/nonlinear probes, CUSUM, kNN distance, AUROC, and the named null controls are standard and well supported, although “a public materials encoder” and “a general/scientific LLM” are not concrete artifacts and several required prediction heads or datasets remain unnamed. The design does include runnable negative-result controls—“shuffled-label nulls,” a “randomly-initialized-model control,” and a “data-density OOD baseline”—but lacks the crucial control of probing the swept variable itself or training probes against alternative arbitrary cut points. Resources receive partial credit for “~10 laws,” “ESM-2 (multiple sizes),” and extraction “at every layer,” but sample counts, sweep resolution, datasets, model checkpoints, and other planning figures are unstated.
